To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
local spreading of the dosage compensation complex is controlled by transcription rate of the roX RNAs.

(1) roX1 transcription rate controls the local spreading of the male-specific lethal (MSL) chromatin remodeling complex in Drosophilamelanogaster; and (2) a short repeat element in the roX1 RNA promotes local spreading.

local spreading of the male-specific dosage compensation complex in flies depends on the rate of roX RNA transcription and that a short sequence motif in the roX RNA is required to achieve high levels of roX RNA production and efficient dosage compensation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of dosage compensation in Drosophil melanogaster.
understanding the mechanism of spreading of the dosage compensation complex along the single male Drosophila X chromosome.
the regulation of dosage compensation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the level of transcription is a major determinant of spreading of the Msl complex from sites of synthesis of roX RNA.
the transcription rate of roX1 RNA is the major factor that controls the extent of local spreading of the dosage compensation complex.
transcription of roX RNAs is required for spreading of the dosage compensation complex in cis from the site of synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of rox1 transcription determines how far MSL proteins spread from sites of rox1 synthesis.
the MSL complex can be recruited by roX RNAs to sites of transcription, but the complex can only spread from sites of rox transcription if the RNA product is present in moderate levels.
roX1 RNA levels determine local spreading of the dosage compensation complex in cis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dosage compensation complex in flies is a highly dynamic entity that responds to the levels of the two noncoding rox RNAs, which in turn depend on transcription rate of the genes encoding the RNAs.
the MSL proteins and roX RNAs can spread in cis, and this process can be regulated.
the level of rox1 transcription is a major determinant of the level of MSL spreading in cis.
